players.product: Neoverse V2/V3 CPU core IP and CSS compute subsystems

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jason Child on licensing: licence and other revenue was a Q1 record, with growth 'driven by strong demand for next-generation architectures and deeper strategic engagements with key customers'. This quarter Arm signed multiple high-value agreements as existing customers renewed long-term licenses: 'Some of the world's largest hyperscalers, automotive and robotics companies, and handset OEMs all secured access to Arm's future roadmap for their next generation of products.' ACV growth continues to be above Arm's long-term expectation for licence revenue growth.
quarterly_data.figure: multiple high-value licence renewals (hyperscalers, automotive and robotics companies, handset OEMs)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jason Child on the Arm AGI CPU path: 'In this quarter, even more customers have wanted to place orders with us', and Arm has made progress to secure additional supply while optimizing customer mix and commercial terms. For FY2027 (calendar 2026) and FY2028 (calendar 2027) the 'supply chain's pretty tight'; 'Maybe there's upside to get to this $2 billion or $2 billion plus', and until supply-chain capacity comes online Arm is 'mostly focused on just trying to get to the $2 billion number next year'. CEO Rene Haas: Arm is working closely with its manufacturing and supply chain partners to expand capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: AGI CPU: 'trying to get to the $2 billion number next year' (CFO)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Jason Child on royalty drivers: cloud AI was again the largest driver of royalty growth; edge AI royalty revenue continued to grow despite a soft smartphone end market; and physical AI 'made a strong contribution to royalty growth, supported by the continued secular expansion of ADAS and autonomous systems built on Arm technology'. Beyond Google, Amazon and NVIDIA there are 'other hyperscalers that are also exceeding their plans'. Child expects any royalty softness this year to be met by at least as much licence revenue, and said most partners 'seem to think that there's going to be stronger recovery in the back half of the year' in smartphones.

CFO Jason Child on spending: the Q1 opex shortfall came from tools such as emulation and cloud spend, not people costs, and investors can 'bank the savings from Q1'; overall opex is then expected to grow by about a mid-single-digit percentage quarter on quarter, as Arm expands its engineering teams for customer demand, next-generation architectures, Compute Subsystems and the Arm AGI CPU product family.

contracts.signal: CEO Rene Haas named Oracle among the Arm AGI CPU customers when walking through the customer base by category: 'We've also just talked about OCI Oracle.' He said the AGI CPU is a great fit for traditional server, head-node and agentic applications, 'and we have customers in all three'.
